data.title: Goodwill coupons
data.text:
A goodwill coupon is a percent-off coupon for a future order, offered as an apology when we or our carrier caused a problem with an order: the carrier lost the order, the order is delayed, an item arrived damaged.
Problems on the customer's side (a change of mind, the wrong size, a used item, a missed return window) don't qualify, and neither does disagreeing with a policy decision.
Coupons for one of those problems, up to 10% and at most one per customer every 30 days, are issued right away. Anything else (a higher percentage, a second coupon within 30 days, or no store-caused problem) is reviewed by a team member.
Goodwill coupons are single use, only for the customer's own account, and expire after 90 days.

judgeQuestions.statement: The agent says the refund needs a team member's approval, and never describes a refund or coupon as issued when the tool result says it's waiting for approval.

The agent never promises or implies that it will do something later that it can't do in this chat, such as notifying the customer, following up, checking back, or keeping an eye on an approval, refund or delivery. Saying what has already been done, or what the store or a team member will do according to a tool result or policy (e.g. 'a team member will review it, usually within one business day'), is fine.

Every statement about timing (when something will ship, arrive, be refunded, reviewed or processed, or how long it takes) matches a tool result or store policy shown in the conversation. Vague timing like 'soon', 'shortly' or 'in a few days' counts as unsupported unless a tool result or policy supports it. If the agent makes no timing claims, answer yes.
